title: Top exterior sheaf commutes with internal duality
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], M a finite locally free sheaf of O_X-modules of constant natural rank d [def-amb-finite-locally-free-module], and M^dual = Hom(M,O_X) its internal dual [def-pur-sheaf-hom]. For the sheafified sectionwise exterior powers [def-sc-sheaf-exterior-power], there exists an isomorphism wedge^d(M^dual) ≅ Hom(wedge^d M,O_X) of ordinary sheaves of O_X-modules. No tensor product, derived category, shift, or extra hypothesis is involved.

proof.text: Choose an open cover trivializing M with rank d. On a subopen of a trivializing open, evaluating an internal Hom section identifies it with a linear functional on sections of M. The inverse sends a functional to the internal sheaf map given by the basis coordinates; restrictions of the basis ensure this inverse is compatible with every smaller open. Exterior sheafification commutes with restriction: both are characterized by the same local maps to sheaves on the localized site. Thus on these opens the exterior sheaves have the sectionwise finite free exterior powers.

Use the increasing-wedge basis of each exterior power. In degree d its basis consists of the single top wedge. The determinant pairing sends the wedge of the dual basis to the dual of that top wedge; hence it is a linear isomorphism. More generally Mathlib exteriorPower.bijective_pairingDual proves bijectivity for finite free modules in every degree. In degree zero both sides are generated by the empty wedge and evaluation is multiplication by one. Over a zero ring the maps are maps of zero modules and remain bijective.

On tensors of pure wedges the formula is the determinant of the evaluations. Evaluation commutes with restriction by naturality of the internal Hom section, and the ring restriction preserves determinants. Wedges span, so the pairings commute with all restrictions. A basis change multiplies the top wedge by its determinant and its dual by the inverse determinant, leaving evaluation unchanged. The local maps therefore agree on overlaps and glue to a morphism from the exterior sheaf of the dual to the internal dual of the exterior sheaf. Their inverses agree by uniqueness and glue too, giving the stated isomorphism. On an empty scheme the assertion is vacuous locally and the maps are the unique isomorphisms.

theorem exteriorSheaf_dual_iso (X : Scheme.{u}) (M : X.Modules) (d : ℕ)
    (hfree : M.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank d) :
    Nonempty ((Scheme.Modules.exteriorSheaf
      (SheafOfModules.homObj (R := X.sheaf) M
        (SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf)) d) ≅
      Scheme.Modules.dual (Scheme.Modules.exteriorSheaf M d))
